01 — ABOUT

From sketch to spec sheet.

Good engineering doesn't end with a CAD model.

I am a Mechanical Engineering student at the Georgia Institute of Technology (Class of 2027) pursuing a minor in Industrial Design, with interests in product development, robotics, and Design for Manufacturing (DFM).

I enjoy designing hardware that is practical to manufacture, intuitive to use, and reliable in practice. To me, engineering is about understanding constraints, evaluating trade-offs, and developing solutions that perform beyond the CAD model.

Every project in this portfolio reflects that mindset. Alongside the final designs, you'll find the calculations, prototype iterations, manufacturing considerations, and engineering decisions that shaped the final product.

SHEET 02 OF 03 — TIKKUN OLAM MAKERS

Custom Assistive Reach Device

TEAMTOM Group Project
ROLEMechanical Engineer
TIMELINEOctober 2025 – November 2025
TOOLSSolidWorks, 3D Printing, Machining
Problem

Design, build, and prototype a device tailored to a specific challenge faced by a "need-knower" — a real person with a real, unmet need, not a hypothetical user.

Approach

Designed an armrest-mounted reach-and-hook mechanism in SolidWorks, then hand-fabricated the plywood armrest and hook hardware and machined the steel hinge in-house. Built and tested three rounds of physical prototypes, refining the hinge fit and strap placement after each round.

Result

A wearable, hinge-actuated reaching aid — built on a strict budget and refined through several rounds of rapid 3D-printed prototypes.

SHEET 03 OF 03 — INTERNSHIP

Self-Serve Check-In Kiosk

COMPANYTAPN
ROLELead Product Engineering Intern
TIMELINEMay 2026 – August 2026
TOOLSSolidWorks, 3D Printing
Problem

Events needed self-serve check-in and registration hardware, but commercial kiosks run $2,000–$5,000+ — out of reach for the events TAPN serves.

Approach

Led end-to-end hardware development: designed the enclosure and casing in SolidWorks with precise tolerancing for manufacturability, then iterated quickly with 3D-printed prototypes to validate the form factor before committing to final production.

Result

A fully functional kiosk delivered in two months, for under $500 — a fraction of commercial equivalents.

03 — MORE WORK

Additional builds.

Smaller projects and coursework that shaped how I design — shown here at a glance.

Individual Project

RoboCup Shell Redesign

Redesigned shells for a six-robot fleet using snap- and friction-fit joints, optimized geometry for 3D printing, and integrated ventilation—eliminating tape-based assembly across the fleet in six weeks.

Individual Project

The '90s Naija Dresser

Culture-inspired 3D-printed shelf — my first hands-on project with GD&T, tolerancing, and design for manufacturing.

Individual Project

The Holiday Music Box

A hand-crank music box combining a moving drawer mechanism with embedded electronics — built to practice integrating motion geometry and electrical components within a single enclosure.

Personal Project

FIFA Club World Cup Trophy

Reverse-engineered and recreated the CWC trophy in SolidWorks + Blender, later featured in TAPN's augmented-reality platform.

Team Project — ME 2110

Mousetrap-Powered Robot

Built an automated pick-and-drop system from 5 mousetraps, 5 rubber bands, and a $120 budget. Ranked 16th of 56 teams as Testing Engineer.

Team Project

Budget Go-Kart for Kids

Designed the powertrain and transmission CAD models for a STEM-outreach go-kart, applying GD&T under a strict $150 budget.

Personal Project

The Unicorn

A 3D-printed ship model inspired by Tintin's The Unicorn — a self-directed exercise in advanced surfacing and complex hull geometry in SolidWorks.
